rq-qz71 — A covered dot steps out of the words

Agreed: Option A, with the no-room case as Variant 1. While the words are open and ◎ Showing is on, a dot whose spot lies under a card or spoken line steps to the nearest free picture just outside the words, as dots already do around the room plate and the buttons. Its name sits beside it when there is room nearby (otherwise dot only, named when pointed at or focused). Pressing it presses its thing. Where no free picture lies near, the dot stands on the nearest edge of the words, half over the card, straight above or below its thing. Hiding the words puts every dot back on its thing.

Elior’s Cottage at 1000×700, after look, two cards open, ◎ Showing.

Red dashed rings show where the hidden dot is today; they are not part of the design.

HearthLanternGrandmotherLantern is wholly under the card: its dot waits just below the card, straight under the lanternShelves steps up into the gap above the cards (dot only: no room for its name nearby)

When the words fill the picture (Variant 1)

A rarer case: the words fill nearly all of the picture (here a long spoken line from Grandmother), so a covered dot has no free picture to step out to.

Grandmother
“Elior! There you are, love. Sit, sit. The bread is nearly cool, and I won’t have you eating it hot again, not after last time. Your grandfather used to say a loaf needs its quiet, same as a person does. Now listen, because I’ve been turning it over all morning: Mira came by at first light, white as flour, saying the hens won’t lay and the well tastes of iron. That’s three things in a week, and three things is a pattern. I want you to go and see her, and take the lantern, because the path by the old mill is dark even at noon this time of year. And mind the shelves on your way out, I’ve stacked the books too high again and one of these days they’ll come down on somebody. Off you go, then. And Elior — come home before the light goes.”
▾ Hide
◎ Showing
No free picture near these things: each dot waits on the edge of the words, straight above or below its thing, and can be pressed there; names show when pointed at or focused

Today, for comparison

The words are open. Hearth, Lantern, Grandmother and Shelves have no dot at all: their spots lie under the cards, so the player cannot see or press them until the words are hidden.
